status_scope: Review complete. Observations include occlusion and lighting limits.

images.observation: Boiler face, circular needle gauge, sight tube, dark access panels, base and overhead pipe couplings are visible.
All three glazed fronts and the timber surround are visible. Several books and a small vessel can be seen through the panes, with a lit doorway to the right.
The gray center elevation shows repeated window bays, a projecting cornice and a broad dark roof with a tank and aerial supports.
The center parapet and window rows read under dusk lighting. A narrow warm strip appears at the base and adjacent panes at right are lit.
The gray brick elevation, rows of rectangular sash windows and shallow roofline are visible against blue sky.
The red center elevation has a recessed middle bay, pale window sills, a parapet outline and a warm hipped rooftop structure on the left.
The pale window rows, U-shaped parapet and warm hipped structure at upper left remain distinguishable.
The three sides of the recessed red-brick bay enclose a strip of blue sky. Window surrounds, sills and horizontal trim remain visible.
A dark roof with repeating dormers tops the far facade. In the lower foreground an orange-edged structure and its parallel rails are visible.
Dormers and pale window rows remain visible above the warmly lit lower framework. Much of the yard is silhouette.
Window and sill rhythms remain readable across the tall facade, with dormers making a stepped silhouette above.
The ochre roof inset and pale border sit above a red elevation with a projecting middle bay. The neighboring windows show warm tones.
Warm inset roof and pale cornice edge are visible over a dim red facade. Nearby panes show isolated warm light.
A projecting stone balcony or balustrade, stacked sash windows and the arched top-center opening read against a split roofline.
The stepped parapet, arched upper windows, tank stands, dishes and guy wires are visible among adjoining rooftops.
Stepped roof, arch tops, tanks and rooftop wires remain visible with warmer adjacent panes.
An inset central stack and arched upper opening divide the pale windows on each side. A dark railing enters along the lower edge.
The broad ochre roof, dark border, tank, dish, fine wires and a prominent cornice are visible above symmetrical sash rows.
Warm light across the broad roof reveals long tank and aerial shadows. The cornice silhouette and pale window rows remain readable below.
A central inset bay with a curved upper window sits between repeated sash rows and an articulated roof cornice under blue sky.
Layered cloud streaks, sloping antenna wires and two dark rooftop tank silhouettes are distinct. Small rooftop fixtures supply orientation, with little roof surface in frame.
Two narrow parallel edge strips recede to the truss silhouette. Small raised shapes form a regular line on the lower side. The slope and strip edges are distinguishable.
The thin retaining edge crosses the dark water and raised right bank. The shot gives little detail across the water.
A dark masonry corner, sidewalk and curb are distinguishable. The blocks behind it fade into fog; most foreground surface detail is in shadow.
Three nearby facade planes step back across the image. The large right block has a regular lit and unlit window grid, with roof and cornice profiles against the clouds.
Roof parapets, rods and wiring sit against the cloud field. A long truss and two raised spans are visible beyond the rooftops to the right.
Curb and storefronts define the street corridor. A dark vehicle now sits in the center foreground; warm storefront glazing remains distinguishable.
A long lighter diagonal band crosses between two dark planes. Its near edge stays readable in the original, with a sharp change in ground tone beneath it and a stepped far horizon.
The low diagonal edge separates the recessed dark field and sloped near ground. The frame establishes silhouette more clearly than surface detail.
The foreground bank edge cuts diagonally across the lower frame. Across the dark span, a line of buildings has alternating light and dark windows with a truss visible at far left.
Tall pale panes and a small interior silhouette are visible behind dark roof trim and masonry. Rooftop tanks and aerials silhouette against the sky.
The two nearest panes show distinct blocky interior shapes. Window trim and red brick remain legible through the foreground steelwork.
Two adjacent gray panes show distinct tall cabinet and low tabletop silhouettes; the warmer panes below show additional interior shapes behind the sash bars.
The gray molded surrounds, arched red-brick window heads and stepped trim are visible. Adjacent cool panes show different interior forms, and warm foreground panes show tables and wall depth.
Foreground brick courses, projecting trim and a partially visible blind give scale. An awning, curved street lamp and receding left roofs mark the street corridor.
Unobstructed fronts show distinct roof silhouettes, masonry, cornices and doors. Divided panes vary between warm and cool tones.
Blue sky and scattered pale cloud patches dominate, with antenna and tank silhouettes at the bottom. The distant rooftop outlines are more distinct than in the other weather views.
A pale layered cloud field and softened silhouettes distinguish this frame from the dry view. Near tank silhouettes and wires remain identifiable at both sides.
A nearly uniform gray sky grades warmer near the horizon. Dark tank shapes and fine mast wires remain visible in the original, with distant roof forms reduced to silhouettes.
The wide view shows water tanks, antennas and rooflines below layered clouds. The bridge truss is legible at the far right, with scattered warm window rectangles across the distant blocks.
Tile, painted upper wall, vertical strip and part of the toilet are visible. The bypass service connection is out of view.
Brick still occludes the fixture. This frame does not verify the visible dumbwaiter.
Warm plank floor, two tables, shelves, doorway and rear radiator are visible. The handheld overlaps the right shelving.
Curtain occupies the left third, with spotlight on tile and painted wall. The toilet is cropped at the lower edge.
Resident and companion have small pose changes. Floor, table, window and fittings remain visible.
The light pool shifts slightly. Floor, table, shelf and radiator remain visible.
The frame shows the sink, pipework, cabinets and wall finish. A strong warm center spot and mottled surround limit fine optical comparisons.
Cabinet and fuse faces are visible. The open door is darker than in the prior capture.
Mailbox rows and mail slot remain recognizable against the dark recessed wall. Small labels are hard to read.
Radiator ribs and valve partly visible below the window beside the side table. A large pale foreground form obscures the left edge; the floor connection is cropped.
Roof landing shows fenced machinery, conduit, stairs and roof sign. Cage bars cross the drive surfaces.
Tank, catwalk and legs silhouette clearly against streaked clouds and surrounding roofs. Dark structural faces limit detailed texture inspection.
Low street view shows a gray front with stone surrounds, red brick fronts with varied arch shapes and warm and cool panes. The right flank is dark.
Lit terminal, wood floor and note board are visible. Slight perspective and lighting differences.
The frame resolves painted wall, glazed tile, toilet cistern, support bars and cropped seat. The deep service fitting is outside the frame.
Colorful pool and curled surface are visible in the warm beam beneath the radiator. A still cannot show the rate or path of flow.
Reddish upright and curled forms stand in front of the radiator under the warm beam. Their silhouette is clear; a still cannot establish motion.
Toaster face, open tray with separate crumb flecks, kettle and nearby vessels are visible.
Station 1 plate and a brass circular part stand out against a dark wall. Fixture detail is limited by low light.
